short: Conv-plus-Transformer EMG encoder (M06) is reused by the 2026 state of the art; the phoneme loss (M02) follows 2018 ultrasound work. Single runs; ablations explain 16.3 of 25.8 points.
position: The paper [@gaddy2021improved] changes two components of the 2020 EMG voicing system [@gaddy2020digital]: a learned convolution-plus-Transformer encoder over minimally filtered EMG (M06) and an auxiliary phoneme loss (M02). M06 departs from the feature-plus-recurrent designs of its time but is standard, not ahead, as every comparison is a single run; it lasted: the 2026 state of the art [later] initializes its encoder from it [@lee2026gets]. M02 is standard: phone-state multi-task training for synthesis was already shown on ultrasound [@toth2018multitask] (credited in §1), though here it gives the largest ablation effect (51.7% against 42.2%, Table 1). Crediting the drop from 68.0% to 42.2% to the three changes outruns the evidence: if their effects add, the ablations account for 16.3 of the 25.8 points (inference), and a modified alignment and a new batching regularizer are never ablated (§2.3). A later Whisper rerun scores 25.74% [@lee2026gets]: recognizer and run move the score more than any ablation (inference).
